answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
Write both factors with the same base: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-4} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{4}\).

So \(x = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2} \times \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{4} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{6}\).

Then \(x^{-2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{-12} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{12}\).

\(2^{12} = 4096\) and \(3^{12} = 531441\).

So, the answer is \(x^{-2} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{12} = \frac{4096}{531441}\).

answers.solution:
Use \((2x + y)^2 = 4x^2 + y^2 + 4xy\).

\((2x + y)^2 = 40 + 4 \times 6 = 40 + 24 = 64\).

So \(2x + y = \pm\sqrt{64} = \pm 8\).

So, the answer is \(2x + y = \pm 8\) (it is 8 when x and y are positive).

answers.label: Q3
answers.solution:
Open the brackets in the numerator: \(17 - 17x - 5x - 60 = -43 - 22x\).

Cross-multiply: \(-43 - 22x = 8(1 - 7x) = 8 - 56x\).

Collect terms: \(56x - 22x = 8 + 43\), so \(34x = 51\).

\(x = \frac{51}{34} = \frac{3}{2}\).

Check: \(1 - 7x = 1 - \frac{21}{2} \neq 0\), so the value is allowed.

So, the answer is \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).

Divide 231228 by 33.

\(33 \times 7006 = 231198\), and \(231228 - 231198 = 30\). So the remainder is 30.

To reach the next multiple of 33 we must add \(33 - 30 = 3\).

Check: \(231231 = 33 \times 7007\).

answers.solution:
The bells toll together again after the LCM of 5, 6, 8 and 12 seconds.

\(5 = 5\), \(6 = 2 \times 3\), \(8 = 2^3\), \(12 = 2^2 \times 3\).

LCM \(= 2^3 \times 3 \times 5 = 120\) seconds.

One hour \(= 3600\) seconds, so they toll together \(\frac{3600}{120} = 30\) times after the start.

So, they toll together 30 times in an hour (excluding the one at the start).

The numbers are \(33\) and \(55\). Check: \(\frac{24}{46} = \frac{12}{23}\).

answers.label: Q10
answers.solution:
A cube of edge 6 m fits along each edge of the cuboid a whole number of times only.

Along 36 m: \(36 \div 6 = 6\) cubes.

Along 15 m: \(15 \div 6 = 2\) cubes (3 m is left over).

Along 8 m: \(8 \div 6 = 1\) cube (2 m is left over).

Number of cubes \(= 6 \times 2 \times 1 = 12\).

(Dividing volumes, \(\frac{36 \times 15 \times 8}{6^3} = 20\), is wrong here, because the left-over pieces 3 m and 2 m thick cannot make whole 6 m cubes.)

So, 12 cubes can be cut.

answers.solution:
In square STUV, UV is a side, and the equilateral triangle UVW stands on UV inside the square.

So \(VW = UV = VS\) (sides of the square and of the equilateral triangle are equal).

\(\angle SVU = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle WVU = 60^\circ\), so \(\angle SVW = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ\).

Triangle SVW is isosceles with \(VS = VW\), so its base angles are equal:

\(\angle VSW = \frac{180^\circ - 30^\circ}{2} = 75^\circ\).

So, \(\angle VSW = 75^\circ\).

\(11.11\% = \frac{1}{9}\) and \(14.28\% = \frac{1}{7}\) (that is \(14\frac{2}{7}\%\)).

Let the cost price be Rs 100. Gain \(\frac{1}{7}\), so selling price \(= 100 \times \frac{8}{7} = \frac{800}{7}\).

Discount \(\frac{1}{9}\) of the marked price, so selling price \(= \frac{8}{9}\) of the marked price.

Marked price \(= \frac{800}{7} \times \frac{9}{8} = \frac{900}{7} = 128\frac{4}{7}\).

Mark-up \(= 128\frac{4}{7} - 100 = 28\frac{4}{7}\) on 100.

So, he marks his goods \(28\frac{4}{7}\%\) (about 28.57%) above the cost price.

Find the LCM: \(16 = 2^4\), \(24 = 2^3 \times 3\), \(36 = 2^2 \times 3^2\), \(54 = 2 \times 3^3\).

LCM \(= 2^4 \times 3^3 = 16 \times 27 = 432\).

The smallest five-digit number is 10000. \(10000 \div 432\) gives quotient 23 and remainder \(10000 - 9936 = 64\).

So the next multiple of 432 is \(432 \times 24 = 10368\) (or \(10000 + (432 - 64) = 10368\)).

So, the answer is 10368.

From the figure, D is on AB, F is on AC, O is on DF, E is on BC, and x is the angle OEB at E.

In triangle AOF, \(AF = OA = OF\), so it is equilateral and \(\angle AFO = 60^\circ\).

DO (that is, the line DF) is parallel to BC, so \(\angle ACB = \angle AFD = 60^\circ\) (corresponding angles).

EO is parallel to CA, and BC cuts both, so \(\angle OEB = \angle ACB = 60^\circ\) (corresponding angles).

(Also \(OD = OF = OA\) makes O the centre of a circle through A, D, F with DF a diameter, which agrees with \(\angle BAC = 90^\circ\).)

So, \(x = 60^\circ\).

Take 3 kg, 4 kg and 5 kg (12 kg in all).

Cost \(= 3 \times 100 + 4 \times 80 + 5 \times 60 = 300 + 320 + 300 = \text{Rs } 920\).

Cost per kg \(= \frac{920}{12} = \frac{230}{3}\) rupees.

Let the express train be L m long; the goods train is 2L m.

Both go the same way, so relative speed \(= 80 - 40 = 40\) km/h \(= 40 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{100}{9}\) m/s.

To overtake, the express covers \(L + 2L = 3L\) in 54 s: \(3L = \frac{100}{9} \times 54 = 600\), so \(L = 200\) m.

To cross a 400 m platform it covers \(200 + 400 = 600\) m at \(80 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{200}{9}\) m/s.

Time \(= 600 \div \frac{200}{9} = 27\) s.

So, the express train takes 27 seconds.

The semicircles APB and CPD have diameters AB = CD = 14 cm, so radius \(r = 7\) cm, and they meet at P.

Area of square \(= 14 \times 14 = 196\) cm\(^2\).

Area of two semicircles \(= 2 \times \frac{1}{2} \pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\) cm\(^2\).

Shaded area \(= 196 - 154 = 42\) cm\(^2\).

So, the area of the shaded region is 42 cm\(^2\).

Growth works like compound interest: \(48400 = 40000\left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right)^2\).

\(\left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{48400}{40000} = \frac{121}{100}\).

\(1 + \frac{R}{100} = \frac{11}{10}\), so \(\frac{R}{100} = \frac{1}{10}\).

\(R = 10\).

So, the rate of growth is 10% per annum.

Call the boxes a, b (top row) and c, d (bottom row).

Rows: \(a + b = 10\) and \(c - d = 8\). Columns: \(a + c = 19\) and \(b + d = 7\).

From \(a + c = 19\) and \(a + b = 10\): \(c - b = 9\).

From \(b + d = 7\): \(d = 7 - b\), so \(c = 8 + d = 15 - b\).

Then \(15 - b - b = 9\), so \(b = 3\), \(a = 7\), \(c = 12\), \(d = 4\).

Check: \(7 + 3 = 10\), \(12 - 4 = 8\), \(7 + 12 = 19\), \(3 + 4 = 7\).

So, the boxes are 7 and 3 in the top row and 12 and 4 in the bottom row.

The height of the cylinder is the width of the paper, \(h = 6\) cm.

The length of the paper, 44 cm, goes round to form the circumference of the base.

\(2\pi r = 44\), so \(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 44\), giving \(r = 7\) cm.

Volume \(= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 6\).

\(= 22 \times 7 \times 6 = 924\) cm\(^3\).

So, the volume of the cylinder is 924 cm\(^3\).

answers.solution:
Read the question as: one full reserved ticket costs Rs 362, and one full plus one half reserved ticket cost Rs 554.

Let the full fare be Rs F and the reservation charge Rs R.

Full reserved ticket: \(F + R = 362\) ... (1)

Half reserved ticket: \(\frac{F}{2} + R\).

One full and one half: \((F + R) + \left(\frac{F}{2} + R\right) = 554\), so \(\frac{F}{2} + R = 554 - 362 = 192\) ... (2)

Subtract (2) from (1): \(\frac{F}{2} = 170\), so \(F = 340\).

From (1): \(R = 362 - 340 = 22\).

So, the reservation charge is Rs 22.

Let room A have x candidates and room B have y.

First condition: \(x - 10 = y + 10\), so \(x = y + 20\) ... (1)

Second condition: \(x + 20 = 2(y - 20)\), so \(x = 2y - 60\) ... (2)

From (1) and (2): \(y + 20 = 2y - 60\), so \(y = 80\).

Then \(x = 80 + 20 = 100\).

Check: 90 and 90 are equal; 120 is double 60.

So, room A has 100 candidates and room B has 80.

answers.solution:
Factorise each part.

\(x^2 + 8x + 12 = (x + 6)(x + 2)\)

\(x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)\)

\(x^2 + 4x - 12 = (x + 6)(x - 2)\)

Dividing means multiplying by the reciprocal:

\(\frac{(x + 6)(x + 2)}{(x - 3)(x - 4)} \times \frac{x - 4}{(x + 6)(x - 2)}\)

Cancel \((x + 6)\) and \((x - 4)\):

\(= \frac{x + 2}{(x - 3)(x - 2)}\)

So, in lowest terms the expression is \(\frac{x + 2}{(x - 2)(x - 3)} = \frac{x + 2}{x^2 - 5x + 6}\).

3 men do the work of 4 women, so 1 man \(= \frac{4}{3}\) women.

7 men \(= 7 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{28}{3}\) women, so 7 men and 5 women \(= \frac{28}{3} + 5 = \frac{43}{3}\) women.

The work needs \(4 \times 43 = 172\) woman-days.

Time \(= 172 \div \frac{43}{3} = 172 \times \frac{3}{43} = 12\) days.

So, 7 men and 5 women take 12 days.

In one hour: tap A fills \(\frac{1}{12}\), tap B fills \(\frac{1}{16}\), and the third tap empties \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the tank.

Net filled in one hour \(= \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{4 + 3 - 6}{48} = \frac{1}{48}\).

answers.finalAnswer: Pie chart with angles Cement 108°, Steel 36°, Bricks 36°, Timber 54°, Labour 90°, Miscellaneous 36°
answers.solution:
The whole circle, \(360^\circ\), stands for 100%, so each 1% is \(3.6^\circ\).

Cement: \(30 \times 3.6 = 108^\circ\)
Steel: \(10 \times 3.6 = 36^\circ\)
Bricks: \(10 \times 3.6 = 36^\circ\)
Timber: \(15 \times 3.6 = 54^\circ\)
Labour: \(25 \times 3.6 = 90^\circ\)
Miscellaneous: \(10 \times 3.6 = 36^\circ\)

Check: \(108 + 36 + 36 + 54 + 90 + 36 = 360^\circ\).

To draw: draw a circle of any convenient radius and one radius as the starting line. With a protractor mark off \(108^\circ\), \(36^\circ\), \(36^\circ\), \(54^\circ\), \(90^\circ\) and \(36^\circ\) in turn, each sector starting where the last one ended. Label each sector with its item and percentage, and give the chart a title.

So, the pie diagram has sectors of \(108^\circ\), \(36^\circ\), \(36^\circ\), \(54^\circ\), \(90^\circ\) and \(36^\circ\).
